title: White House launches Arcade.gov with computer game that lets players 'deport' migrants
summary:
The White House announced the launch of what it called "Arcade.gov," a website of five versions of classic computer games promoting the president's agenda.
One of the games, "Rio Run," a variation on the popular Snake computer game, has players "deport" migrants along the Rio Grande along the U.S.-Mexico border.
In "Build the Wall," a Tetris-like game, players are encouraged to "protect the border from the coming horde" of zombies.
The White House did not respond to multiple questions about whether any contractors were hired or taxpayer funds used for the project.
In a post on Instagram, the Tetris Company said it was not involved in the creation of the White House game and said "we take copyright infringement very seriously."

title: UK gov’t condemns masked anti-immigrant protesters blocking Dover port
summary:
Ferry traffic at UK’s largest international port was briefly halted as ‘stop the boats’ protesters blocked approaching roads.
Dozens of masked people protesting Channel migrant crossings have blocked access to the port of Dover, briefly halting ferry traffic between England and France.
On Saturday morning, the Port of Dover said all traffic in and out was “stopped due to an ongoing public order incident”.
The National Highways agency said the protest blocked roads to the port and caused a 6.4km traffic jam on Saturday morning.
Dover is Britain’s largest international ferry port.

title: Dutch artist responds to the White House's Build the Wall game with Build that Bridge
summary:
A Dutch artist has released Build that Bridge, a free browser game built as a direct response to Build the Wall, the Tetris-style minigame the White House launched on Arcade.Gov last week.
Whereas the White House version has players stack blocks into a wall, artist and social designer Wouter Sieuwerts's version, Build that Bridge, uses the same mechanics in reverse: clearing lines grows a bridge from both riverbanks toward the middle.
"Just as the colonisation of America was turned into child's play, the White House now makes a game out of excluding migrants," Sieuwerts said.
So for everyone who would rather build bridges than walls, I made Build that Bridge.
Build that Bridge is free to play at buildthatbridge.eu, with no ads, no data collection, and no account required.

title: White House launches Arcade.gov, a minigame site parodying immigration enforcement and border security
summary:
The White House has launched Arcade.Gov, a website of browser minigames built around Donald Trump's immigration and border policies.
As spotted by IGN, the site includes mini-games based on games like Flappy Bird.
A snake-like game called Rio Run wants you to collect a chain of prisoners in orange jumpsuits, tallying a "deported" count at the end of each run.
Videos posted to social media parody the boot-up sequence animations of retro consoles like PS2 and Xbox 360, alongside a Sega-esque logo reading "Maga".
It's the latest example of the Trump administration using gaming culture for political messaging, a pattern that has prompted objections from rights holders including Nintendo and The Pokémon Company.
